memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And now I bring the firstfruits of the soil that you, Lord, have given me.' Place the basket before the Lord your God and bow down before him. Then you and the Levites and the foreigners residing among you shall rejoice in all the good things the Lord your God has given to you and your household." — Deut 26:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The worshipper finishes his story and returns to the present: "And now I bring the firstfruits." His giving flows naturally out of remembering God's grace. Because he recalled all God had done, offering the basket back was pure joy.

Then comes a beautiful command — rejoice. And not alone. The Israelite, the Levite (who had no land of his own), and the foreigner living among them were all to celebrate together in God's goodness. Worship overflowed into shared joy, and God made sure the vulnerable and the outsider were included in the feast.

This is the heart of God. His blessings are never meant to be hoarded privately; they are meant to be enjoyed in community, with room made for those who have less. True gratitude always opens its hands to others.

When we grasp how much God has given us in Christ, our worship becomes joyful and generous rather than stingy and self-focused. We give, and then we rejoice — and we make sure others can rejoice with us. The gospel creates a family where the Levite and the foreigner, the insider and the outsider, all celebrate the same good God together (Rom 15:7).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is giving to God a joy for me, or a burden?
2. Who around me — especially the overlooked — could I include in God's goodness?
3. How can my gratitude become generosity this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for all the good things You have poured into my life. Make my giving joyful and my heart generous, and help me include others in the blessings You give. Amen.
